# CX-from-abi: the shape `ortho new adapter --from-abi` generates

**Status: decided, 26 November 2026,** by Goal 16's ✍️ checks author for unit A1 (#1164), started by the money lane's 🧭 lead,
under AGENTS.md "Who decides". The checks pin it; the 🔨 builder builds to it; the hand-written adapters A2 (`@orthograph/erc20`,
#1162), A3 (`@orthograph/safe`, #1161) and A4 (`@orthograph/zodiac-roles`, #1163) are written to it now and regenerated by it
once it lands (`CX-safe.md`, sections 3 and 4).

## The problem

`CX-safe.md` has the three adapters hand-written "to the shape `--from-abi` will generate", built in parallel with A1's checks,
so the shape had to be fixed before any of them is written. Parked Goal 12 had drafted one (`ST2-abi-adapters.md` and the
checks in #497, on `goal-12/st2-02-check`, never merged): a package `@orthograph/adapters-abi` for the generator and its runtime,
`@orthograph/erc20` generated by it, one ABI per adapter, errors as `Blueprint.error`s. Three things changed since: chain-evm
now has the codec Goal 12 asked for (`Abi.encodeCall`, `decodeResult`, `encodeDeploy`, `refusal`, `ChainPort.read`, Goal 18
slice 9); A1 owns a module in `packages/generators` and in `packages/cli`, not a package (`CX-safe.md` section 4); and the Safe
and Roles adapters each hold several contracts (the Safe, its proxy factory, MultiSend; the Roles modifier and Zodiac's module
proxy factory).

## The call

The whole shape is `packages/generators/src/modules/abi/README.md`; in short:

1. **One adapter, one or more contracts, one ABI file each.** `--from-abi <file>` is given once per contract; the contract is
   named by the file's base name (`ERC20.json` is `ERC20`). The file is a bare ABI, or an artifact holding one (forge's and
   Hardhat's `{ abi, bytecode: { object } }`, or `{ abi, bytecode }`). Bytecode makes the contract deployable: its stand-in.
2. **The files.** `abi/<Contract>.json` (the input, normalised, so the folder regenerates from itself), `src/generated/<Contract>.ts`
   per contract and `src/generated/index.ts`, all generated; `src/index.ts` (the descriptor), `blueprint/README.md` (a mount
   reads the plugin's `blueprint/`) and `package.json`, scaffolds. Hand-written code (the Safe's address prediction, its SafeTx
   typed data, its `GS0xx` string reverts, the world starters, the Roles budget compiler) goes in files of the adapter's own
   beside `src/generated/`, never in it.
3. **Explicit types,** Goal 12's names and mapping (`<Fn>Args`, `<Fn>Answer`, `<Event>EventArgs`, `<Error>Fields`; `uint` and
   `int` to `bigint`, `address` to `Address`, `bytes` to `Hex`, arrays to `ReadonlyArray`, tuples to interfaces, an indexed
   dynamic event input to the `Hex` of its topic; overloads `<name>_<n>`). One change: a tuple is named by the type that holds
   it plus its own name (`BoxedArgsB`, `BoxedAnswerOut`), so an input's and an output's tuples never meet. Two more: an
   unnamed input is named by its position, `arg0`, as typechain names it, where Goal 12 refused it: Safe 1.4.1's
   `approvedHashes` and `signedMessages` and Roles 2.1.1's `allowances`, `HashAlreadyConsumed`, `HashExecuted` and
   `HashInvalidated` have one (public mappings), and refusing them would make A3 and A4 hand-edit the published ABIs (their
   authors, 26 November 2026). And bytecode still holding a library's `__$…$__` placeholder (Roles' mastercopy) is refused
   with its own message: link it first, or leave it out and stand the contract in by hand, as A4's world starter does. The hostile pass on the checks
   fixed four more: a lone unnamed array of tuples answers `ReadonlyArray<<F>AnswerItem>`; an overloaded error's class is
   `<name>_<n>`, tag and all; an error may be named as an import (`Effect`, `Address`) and the module still compiles; and an
   error named as one of the module's own exports (`Refusal`, `Chain`, `abi`, …) is refused.
4. **The calls run on chain-evm, untyped below and typed above.** `at({ port, address, from? })` holds one call per function: a
   `view` or `pure` one reads (`ChainPort.read`, decoded); any other writes (`prepare`, `simulate`, `sign`, `submit`, answering
   the `Submission`), a `payable` one taking `{ value }`. The generated module imports only `effect` and
   `@orthograph/chain-evm/device`; no viem leaves chain-evm (M1.30's lint).
5. **A revert of the contract's own error is its class.** Each ABI error is `class X extends Data.TaggedError("X")<XFields>`,
   and a write or read that reverts with its selector fails as that class, fields decoded, nothing sent and no nonce kept. Any
   other revert stays chain-evm's `ChainError`. Not `Blueprint.error`: an operation's errors need exit codes and refusal
   codes, which M6.10 gives (`refusals.lock`); an adapter that needs one today maps the class in its handler.
6. **The descriptor** is `Blueprint.adapter({ description, calls, standIn })`: one `Blueprint.call({ mode: "effect" })` per
   function under its contract (`calls.ERC20.transfer`), and the stand-in a process when any contract has bytecode. It mounts:
   `ortho check` passes with it mounted (e2e/m2 check 11). Events as an adapter's `on:` are E1's (#1165).
7. **The three adapters are held to it.** `regenerate.test.ts` regenerates `packages/erc20`, `packages/safe` and
   `packages/zodiac-roles` from their own `abi/` and compares the generated files byte for byte. It is on the ratchet list
   until each package exists and A1's builder has regenerated it.

Not taken from Goal 12: the separate `adapters-abi` package (A1 owns modules, and the runtime is chain-evm's now); generating
`erc20` in A1 (A2 hand-writes it in parallel); a conformance report against a cloud contract (no network now; the Anvil check is
the conformance); refusing `payable` (the Safe's `execTransaction` is payable). Taken, and credited in the files: the names, the
mapping and the refusals.

## The evidence

The checks (`packages/generators/src/modules/abi/`, `packages/cli/src/modules/from-abi/`, `e2e/m2/11-new-adapter-from-abi.test.ts`)
were passed by a throwaway build of this shape on 26 November 2026, against the fixture `Probe.sol` (solc 0.8.30) on Anvil:
calls, events, typed reverts, the nonce after a refusal, and an app mounting the generated adapter through `ortho check`. The
throwaway is not committed; the pull request gives the runs.
